title: Find the integrating factor
text: Put the equation in the form $$y'+p\left(x\right) y=q(x)$$, then multiply by the integrating factor so the left side becomes the derivative of the integrating factor times $$y$$.

title: Integrate and solve
text: In standard form $$y'-\frac{y}{1+x^2}=\frac{-1}{1+x^2}$$, and the integrating factor is $$e^{\left(-\arctan\left(x\right)\right)}$$. This gives $$e^{\left(-\arctan\left(x\right)\right)} y=e^{\left(-\arctan\left(x\right)\right)}+C$$, so $$y=1+C e^{\arctan\left(x\right)}$$. $$y(0)=0$$ gives $$C=-1$$.
